correctness.rationale: For every full plane binary tree with n>=2 consecutive leaves and strictly positive weight at every internal-node simplex, each maximizing simplex leaf is unique almost surely; sum-of-support equalities prove distinct internal winner patterns expose distinct vertices. Decompose a uniform permutation into the independent interleaving of child rankings and their internal rankings: each node winner bit is independent with probabilities a/(a+b),b/(a+b). Therefore Gaussian cone angles factor and 2^(n-1) C(T)=product_v[1+((a_v-b_v)/(a_v+b_v))^2]. A lowest imbalanced internal node has two perfect dyadic child subtrees and relative imbalance >=1/3; hence a factor >=10/9. If precisely one node is imbalanced with ratio two, its parent could not remain balanced because its non-power-of-two subtree size forces an imbalanced sibling; thus the node must be the root. Perfect trees are the sole uniform-angle case. This proves both infinite claims, exact equality family and n=6 comparisons independently of finite enumeration. Independently enumerated all 1,2,5,14,42,132,429 plane shapes at n=2..8 and checked the gap with Fraction arithmetic, including exactly two ordered 10/9 extremizers at n=3 and n=6. Scope excludes zero weights, incomplete internal-node building sets and affinely distorted Euclidean metrics.

value.rationale: Normalized Gaussian vertex-collision is a canonical geometric measure of unequal normal-cone mass within a fixed combinatorial cube. The universal forbidden interval and complete dyadic equality classification reveal a structural rigidity phenomenon, realized in infinitely many dimensions, and expose a counterintuitive six-leaf case in which an unequal root split gives more uniform angles than a balanced root. This is a motivated family-wide geometric invariant, not a table recomputation.

limitations: Full binary trees with every internal-node simplex present and strictly positive weight; no affine-invariant conclusion for arbitrary cubes or arbitrary nestohedra.
